subject: Learning Methods
title: Why Peer Teaching Works
description: A quick, practical guide to Why Peer Teaching Works.

hook.text: Students who taught a peer performed better on exams than those who received traditional instruction alone.

buildup.text: Peer teaching activates what Vygotsky called the zone of proximal development.

discovery.text: A peer who learned something explains it in relatable terms. They remember what confused them and address it directly.

twist.text: The teacher gains even more than the learner. Preparing and explaining reorganizes their knowledge at a deeper level.

climax.text: Form study pairs where each person teaches alternate topics. Both benefit. The teacher often benefits more.

punchline.text: The teacher gains more than the student. Teach to learn.

quiz.question: Why is a peer often a better explainer than an expert teacher?
options: They remember what was confusing and address it directly
